items_missed: No agenda statement. The call opened 'Hello, good afternoon Arden here from Einstein. Sorry moving. How can I help?' and went straight into zip-code collection — the customer was never told what the next 7 minutes would cover or how long it would take. (Sections 3-7 are auto-credited under the walkthrough-scheduler rule, but the agenda is graded and was absent.)
Never asked 'How are you today?' or any warm-up question before starting data collection.

Customer's name never used once in the entire call. Arden said 'ma'am' roughly twenty times but never 'Sue' — short of the 3+ standard, and especially costly with an older customer who volunteered personal detail ('my husband... he passed away but it was Ed').

Name and email captured incorrectly and never cleanly verified. Arden first wrote 'R-U-S-S,' then read the address back as 'S-U-E-E-D-R-U-F-F' and then said 'and then at Gmail @yahoo.com.' The walkthrough link is the entire deliverable of this call and the address it goes to was left ambiguous on the recording.

Never asked about stairs or floors at either end. The destination is Presbyterian Village North, a senior-living community — floor, elevator, and long interior carries were never established, and a virtual walkthrough of the origin house will not surface any of them.

No access-concern probe at all — no elevator, no parking, no loading dock, no COI/certificate-of-insurance question. Senior-living and multi-family destinations routinely require a COI and a reserved dock window; if that surfaces on move day the crew is standing still on the clock.

Never asked about packing needs, even though the customer raised boxes twice unprompted: 'I've got so many boxes in here, there are a lot of boxes and I had a lot of books.' A 2,400 sq ft house full of book boxes is the clearest packing-services opening on this call and it went unworked.
No probe for additional rooms (garage, attic, storage unit, patio), storage stops, or additional stops.

No moving-stressor question. The customer flagged her own worry directly — 'I have a piano, a grandfather clock and a cedar chest, and a dresser. And those items, you know, are heavy and and you have to be careful with them' — and Arden's entire response was 'I see and when do you want this?' The stated fear was not acknowledged, not reassured, and is not confirmed as noted anywhere.

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned, despite the piano and grandfather clock being raised as the customer's explicit concern. This is a bonus-section miss here rather than a pricing miss, but it is the single most obvious unspoken line in the call.

Clarity and pace were a problem. Heavy filler throughout ('Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.', 'one second, one second', 'We mm-hmm one second'), a self-interrupting greeting, and 'Okay, now in order. Hello, ma'am.' mid-call. Roughly a quarter of the call is the email-spelling loop.

Availability framed backwards: 'we don't have availability on the ninth we do the latest availability I can offer ma'am. Is Friday the eleventh.' The customer asked for the 9th or 10th, so the 11th is the *earliest* opening, not the latest — the wording invites confusion on the one commitment made.

Customer offered a real buying signal that was not captured: 'if something canceled, you want to come earlier, well, I would be ready. Yeah, I would be ready earlier.' No offer to add her to a cancellation/waitlist and no confirmation that flexibility would be noted on the record.
top_strength: Arden read the call correctly and made the right structural decision fast. Told it was a 2,400 sq ft house but 'I don't have a lot to move. I've got a lot of boxes, I have a piano, a grandfather clock and a cedar chest,' she did not force a phone estimate onto a job whose scope she could not see — she said 'since we're not going to be moving the entire home in just few items... we can set up a virtual walkthrough so you can tour me around your house,' got explicit agreement, and closed a specific slot: Monday 11:00 AM, confirmed twice, with the mechanics spelled out plainly ('I'm gonna send you a link, you just have to click on it and we're just gonna do like a FaceTime'). She also pre-loaded the walkthrough to make it productive rather than exploratory: 'before we do the virtual walkthrough if you can count the boxes already and have an inventory. So at least it will be smooth because you already have a list of items.' And she volunteered the no-deposit differentiator unprompted at exactly the right moment — right as she described the path to booking: 'you don't have to pay any deposit. Okay, you only pay after the actual move is done.' Her one genuine warmth moment landed, too: when the customer apologized for slowing down to read her own address, saying 'I'm old and I can't see,' Arden answered 'It's okay ma'am it's okay' — and the customer signed off with 'Thank you hun.' On the narrow job of this call type — qualify, route to walkthrough, lock a time — she got the outcome.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix is verification of the two data points this entire call depends on. The only deliverable Arden owes Sue is a link, and both the spelling of her name and her email were left unresolved on the recording — 'R-U-S-S' first, then 'S-U-E-E-D-R-U-F-F,' then 'and then at Gmail @yahoo.com.' The line she needed, once, slowly, at the end: 'Sue, let me read this back to you so I get it exactly right — S-U-E-E-D-R-U-F-F at yahoo dot com, and I'm sending the walkthrough link there right now while we're on the phone. Can you tell me when it lands?' Confirming receipt live turns a hoped-for Monday appointment into a confirmed one. Second priority: she was handed the customer's stated fear and skipped past it. 'Those items are heavy and you have to be careful with them' about a piano and a grandfather clock deserved 'That's exactly what I want to look at on Monday, and it's also what our No Worries Damage Coverage is for — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage. I'm noting the piano and the grandfather clock on your file right now so the crew plans for them.' Practice pairing every stated worry with the differentiator that answers it. Third, use her name — zero uses across seven minutes, all 'ma'am,' with a customer who was clearly warm and told Arden about her late husband. Operational flags to close before Monday: (1) the destination is Presbyterian Village North, a senior-living community — a COI, an elevator or floor, a loading-dock window, and a long interior carry are all live possibilities and none were asked about; a virtual walkthrough of the origin will not reveal any of them, so those questions have to be added to the Monday agenda explicitly. (2) The customer twice emphasized 'a lot of boxes' and 'a lot of books' and was never offered packing services or asked whether the boxes are already packed and sealed — that is both a revenue miss and an estimate-accuracy risk. (3) She said she would be ready earlier if something cancelled; get her on the cancellation list. (4) The 11th was described as the 'latest' availability when it is the earliest — restate the date plainly on Monday so there is no ambiguity about what was held.
phone_presence_notes: One real warmth moment that landed — 'It's okay ma'am it's okay' when the customer apologized for being slow to read her address, and the customer closed with 'Thank you hun' — but the rest was filler-heavy and transactional ('Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.', 'one second, one second'), her name was never used, and the customer's stated worry about her piano and grandfather clock drew only 'I see and when do you want this?'
audio_review_reason: Transcript turns are interleaved out of order (a block of the customer's 'Okay / Because / Yes' responses is stacked at the end rather than in place), and the name/email exchange is unresolvable from text — Arden reads back 'R-U-S-S,' then 'S-U-E-E-D-R-U-F-F,' then 'at Gmail @yahoo.com.' Audio is needed to confirm what address she actually recorded and whether the walkthrough link went to the right place.
